title: On Approving the plan after long debate
subtitle: 国家公民 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 国家公民（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·国家与公民）
meta: 主题语境：国家公民（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·国家与公民）　|　核心词汇：approve　|　正文 361 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 approve 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1973 the counsellor ① approved the plan after long debate for the whole place, and every listener in the garden said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three evenings on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the counsellor ② approves the plan after long debate without a word of thanks without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ approve the plan after long debate at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ approved the plan after long debate before — a line in the journal for June 1967 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Approving the plan after long debate for the whole place, the counsellor said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the letter at the far bench, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ approve of what the young men did without a word of thanks, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Approve of what the young men did at once and never mention it again.

By 1980 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the journal, and a new listener from the next garden ⑧ approves of what the young men did for the whole place every evening without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the bench, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ approved the plan after long debate again when nobody else would.

⑩ To approve the plan after long debate, my mother said in 1985, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the garden remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the garden forgets, somebody approves the plan after long debate without a word of thanks again and somebody must approve the plan after long debate for the whole place all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 批准（一般过去式 approved the plan after long debate：1973 年谈心人头一回这样做，替所有人）
B. v. 批准（一般现在 approves the plan after long debate：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 批准（不定式 to approve the plan after long debate：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 批准（过去完成时 had approved the plan after long debate：1967 年六月的心记上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 批准（动名词 approving the plan after long debate 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 赞成（approve of what the young men did：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去赞成年轻人做的那些事）
G. v. 赞成（approve of what the young men did：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 批准（后段两处：新来的倾听者照例 approves of what the young men did，而母亲又一次 approved the plan after long debate）

answers.why: approve 意为“批准”，1973 年谈心人替所有人批准久议之后批准那个计划，那是小园里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 approved。
approve 意为“批准”，自那以后谈心人不图一句谢把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 approves。
approve 意为“批准”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯批准久议之后批准那个计划”，此处为不定式 to approve the plan after long debate。
approve 意为“批准”，心记里 六月 那行字说明早在 1980 年之前就有人批准过，故用过去完成时 had approved。
approve 意为“批准”，谈心人说“批准久议之后批准那个计划这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 approving the plan after long debate 作主语。
approve 意为“赞成”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去赞成年轻人做的那些事”，should ever 之后用原形 approve of what the young men did。
approve 意为“赞成”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻赞成年轻人做的那些事（approve of what the young men did at once），以后再也不要提起。
approve 意为“批准”，新来的倾听者每个黄昏都照例赞成年轻人做的那些事，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 approves。
approve 意为“批准”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次替所有人批准久议之后批准那个计划，用一般过去式 approved 叙述。
approve 意为“批准”，结尾那句是母亲 1985 年的话：要批准久议之后批准那个计划，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和小园记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 approve 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1973 the counsellor approved the plan after long debate for the whole place, and nobody in the garden forgot it.
Even now the counsellor approves the plan after long debate without a word of thanks whenever the garden asks.
Approving the plan after long debate for the whole place, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever approve of what the young men did without a word of thanks, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new listener from the next garden approves of what the young men did for the whole place every evening, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother approved the plan after long debate again, and the garden remembered that half.
